status.label: Retest Dvorak Ctrl-J/K mappings on the current build
status.detail: On v0.86, Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V work intermittently with a Dvorak layout and custom Sofle V2/QMK keyboard; old logs were reviewed without a clear finding.

judgment.rationale: The reporter lists a Dvorak layout, a custom Sofle V2/QMK keyboard, Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V mappings, and intermittent failures in Vivaldi. A current-build test is absent. A maintainer already reviewed the attached 2024 report and found no clear log signal, and the reporter supplied the keyboard model; do not ask for those same details again. The next discriminator is whether one exact mapping fails in current Vivaldi and a plain text editor.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.86.0, Dvorak layout, and Vivaldi 7.0.3495.26.
The reporter maps Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V; Ctrl-J sometimes passes through as Ctrl-J.
The reporter identified a custom split Sofle V2 keyboard with QMK firmware.
A 2024 /bugreport was attached and a maintainer said nothing stood out in the logs.
judgment.recommended_action: Retest one exact mapping on v0.102.3001 in Vivaldi and a plain text editor; if it still fails, provide a new /bugreport captured immediately after failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported intermittent pass-through is a Keyboard Manager defect if it still occurs, but current behavior and whether failure is browser-specific are unknown.

proposed_fixes.title: Apply Dvorak Ctrl-J/K remaps consistently
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager may translate Dvorak-layout input inconsistently for the custom QMK keyboard, allowing the original Ctrl-J/K chord to pass through; no current trace confirms this.
plan: Retest Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V on v0.102.3001 in Vivaldi and a plain text editor.
Record the active Dvorak input layout and whether the original chord or mapped output occurs in each application.
If current failure is confirmed, trace layout-aware key translation and add a focused regression test for the failing chord.
verification: Verify Ctrl-J and Ctrl-K always produce their mapped outputs in Vivaldi and a plain text editor.
Verify unrelated Dvorak and numpad input is unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The report includes a custom keyboard and old logs, but it is from 0.86.0 and no current reproduction shows whether the issue is layout or browser specific.

issue_context.summary: Dvorak Ctrl-J/K remaps reportedly fail intermittently on a custom Sofle V2/QMK keyboard.
known_information: Mappings are Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V; Ctrl-J sometimes passes through.
The keyboard is a custom Sofle V2 running QMK firmware.
A prior diagnostic archive was reviewed without a clear log finding.
inferences: Keyboard layout translation or interaction with the custom firmware may be involved, but neither is established.
issue_context.analysis: The device and old diagnostic have already been supplied. Retest the exact mappings on the current build in both Vivaldi and a plain text editor; ask for new diagnostics only if a current failure occurs.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and all four comments, including the reporter keyboard model and prior diagnostic exchange.
The maintainer already reviewed the v0.86 report and found no clear log signal.
Confirmed there is no v0.102.3001 reproduction.

information_gaps.information: Whether the intermittent Ctrl-J/K remap failure reproduces on v0.102.3001.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest the same mappings on v0.102.3001.

information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes browser-specific input handling from general layout/key translation.
information_gaps.information: Whether the same mapping failure occurs in Vivaldi and a plain text editor with the Dvorak layout active.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Test Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V once in Vivaldi and once in a plain text editor, recording whether the original or mapped chord occurs.

information_gaps.why_needed: The existing v0.86 report was reviewed without a clear finding and cannot establish current engine state.
information_gaps.information: A fresh archive if the failure recurs on v0.102.3001.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Immediately after reproducing on the current build, comment /bugreport.

comment.body:
Thanks for identifying the Dvorak layout, the Sofle V2/QMK keyboard, the two mappings, and the prior diagnostic archive. A maintainer already reviewed that old report without a clear log finding, so there is no need to resend it.

Could you please:
1. Retest Ctrl-J to Ctrl-C and Ctrl-K to Ctrl-V on v0.102.3001 in Vivaldi and a plain text editor, and report whether the original or mapped chord occurs.
2. If either mapping still fails, comment /bugreport immediately after the failure.
This will distinguish a current layout/key translation issue from a Vivaldi-specific behavior.
